key_insight: The paper shows that nonsmooth nonconvex composite optimization can achieve the same optimal oracle complexity as the noncomposite case by extending online-to-nonconvex conversion to handle a convex regularizer directly.
engineering_relevance: This provides a theoretically optimal optimization framework for constrained learning and regularized neural network training when only stochastic gradients or function values are available.
method: Uses online-to-nonconvex conversion to select update directions via an online learner.
Introduces new composite losses that keep the regularizer in its original form instead of linearizing it.
Applies a low-regret variant of online mirror descent to obtain stationarity guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports complexity guarantees of O(δ^{-1}ε^{-3}) stochastic gradient queries and O(dδ^{-1}ε^{-3}) function-value queries, matching optimal rates for the noncomposite setting, plus numerical experiments.
watch_item: The guarantee depends on a Goldstein-type stationarity notion and may be sensitive to the choice of δ, ε, and the practical cost of the online-learning subroutine.
paper_title: Composite Online-to-Nonconvex Conversion with Optimal Oracle Complexity
